Explain.

As hon. gentlemen know, there is a provision in the Criminal Code in regard to lotteries. Section 236 of the Criminal Code was amended, and special provision was inserted to permit churches or eleemosynary institutions to hold lotteries where the prize was of less value than $50. They were permitted under this provision to conduct a raffle. The purpose of the bill is to cut out that exception, on the ground that if the church of this country is to be a model for the discipline and morality of the country they should set a good example to others. Hon. members will quite appreciate the force of the old maxim which declares that the church is the teacher of the laws and the dictator of morals. What is wrong for an individual is wrong for the church.

The committee will note that British Columbia and the Yukon are put together. As was indicated' last year, the Yukon is not organized as a province, and the interests of the returned men residing in that territory, it was felt, might be better served if the province of British Columbia and the Yukon were joined in the administration of these two allotments. In this regard, however, certain representations have been made to me by different persons having an immediate interest in the welfare of the Yukon; returned men and members of this House who have taken an interest in the matter have represented that, from the Yukon point of view, it would be preferable if the share that fell to that district were allotted1 to it directly instead of forming a part of the allotment to British Columbia for use in both the province and the Yukon. Personally I have no objection to this being done, I cannot look unfavourably on any such proposal; and, if it is the desire of the committee, I shall introduce an amendment to the bill to provide that the Yukon shall have its share separately. If this is done, however, some local committee or board will have to be appointed for the disposal of the allotment, whatever it may be.
The percentages which are set out in the resolution are arrived at on three bases,-the percentage of enlistments, the percentage of discharges, and the percentage of pensioners in each province or territory as the case may be. This has been deemed by the royal commission the fairest way of dealing with the fund, and we have adhered to the principle this year as we did' last year. The figures are somewhat different, but they are correct to date, having been subjected to a close review by the Department of National Defence. These, I think, are the only comments that seem necessary at the moment, but I shall be pleased1 to give hon. gentlemen any information that may be in my possession.

speechtext:
Perhaps the minister
would recognize it if I read it to him? He will have more difficulty I think in defending it than in recognizing it. The order in council is dated September 18, 1924, and is as follows:
Certified copy of a minute of a meeting of the Committee of the Privy Council approved by His Excellency the Governor General on the 18th September, 1924.
The committee of the Privy Council have had before them a report dated 12th September, 1924, from the Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment representing that the Assistant Deputy Minister of the Department of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment is the trustee of a fund known as the Disablement Fund which was contributed by patriotic citizens mainly during the years 1915 and 1916 and that this fund is being used generally for the purpose of small loans to pensioners and others who are in need of immediate assistance and who, in the opinion of the departmental investigations, would benefit by such assistance.
The Dominion Veterans' Alliance, which represents the various veterans' organizations throughout Canada has for a considerable time past maintained a service bureau in Ottawa for the purpose of assisting former
members of the forces in the presentations of claims in respect of pension, medical treatment and other matters. It is stated by the officers of the Alliance that the service given involves considerable expenditure.
On the introduction of a bill to parliament at the last session to deal with the canteen funds now in the hands of the government provision was made for the setting aside of the sum of one hundred thousand dollars to be applied by a board of trustees to the maintenance of an adjustment bureau in the city of Ottawa. It was intended to utilize the Dominion Veterans' Alliance as the adjustment bureau under the provisions of that bill. (Wing to the fact that this measure was introduced during the last few days of the parliamentary session it failed to become law and consequently the moneys which would have been available for the assistance of the Dominion Veterans' Alliance still remain in the hands of the Receiver General. It is proposed to re-introduce the bill early next session.
The minister further represents that in order to enable the Dominion Veterans' Alliance to continue its activities a loan of five thousand dollars ($5,000) was made by the trustee of the Disablement Fund in June, 1924, and that it is now proposed that a further loan of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) be made, subject to reimbursement of the disablement fund should any moneys be appropriated by parliament for the benefit of the alliance or should the proposed allocation from the canteen funds be made.
The minister states that a further loan of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) is being made out of the Disablement Fund to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance, payable as to five thousand dollars ($5,000) on the 1st of October, 1924, and as to five thousand dollars ($5,000) on the 1st of January, 1925, and he recommends that the trustees who may be appointed after the passage of the canteen funds bill at the next session of parliament be requested to reimburse the Disablement Fund the amount ot fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) out of any moneys transferred to such trustees under the authority of the said bill.
The committee concur in the foregoing recommendation and submit the same for approval.
E. J. Lemaire,
Clerk of the Privy Council.
On the recommendation of the minister the government effected a misappropriation of trust funds-admitted on the face of the document to be a misappropriation to the extent of $25,000-trust funds, known generally as the Carruthers fund, contributed by patriotic citizens, for certain definite purposes specified in the trust. Because the government did not get their bill through parliament under which they hoped to support this Dominion Veterans' Alliance, they take the money out of this trust fund and hand it over to the Alliance, and then say, "We will depend on parliament recouping the trust fund." They give, as the reason why parliament has not already made good the breach of trust, that the bill was presented too late last session, and therefore did not pass; the order in council recites that it was because the bill came so late to the House that it did not pass. But the Prime Minister declared that it did not pass because of the obduracy of the Tory
Canteen Funds

Senate, and because of that obduracy he mounted his charger, raised his sword, and proceeded through Canada on a campaign to clip the Senate's wings. Now the order in council says parliament approved of the bill all right, and it was only because it reached the Senate late that it could not get through. Anticipating the will of (parliament, the government passes the money out of the treasury before parliament has any say about it at all-not only passes it out of the treasury, but passes it out of a specific trust fund.
Now will the minister give his opinion of that as an example to the people of Canada? I wonder how that would appear before the depositors, say, of the Home Bank at the present time? What would their opinion be of conduct of this kind on the part of trustees? There is no question as to the facts. No man need start to argue that the use of the funds for that purpose was in accordance with the terms of the trust. If it was, we would not need an order; if it was, the trustee could do it; if it was, we would never suggest a return. The minister says that parliament is going to be asked to return this money; that parliament would have done it before only we were so slow about getting it through the House. The fact is that parliament rejected it. Parliament acted on it; this House passed it; the other House rejected it. But the government is above parliament in both its branches; and of course this is all a part of the great programme of "restoring responsible government to Canada."

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: The trustee is recited to be the Assistant Deputy Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment. He is the trustee, but the government orders him to dig into his trust funds and apply the moneys to purposes not within the purview of the trust at all, to assist what they call an "adjustment bureau" of the Dominion Veterans' Alliance, And they justify it by saying that parliament will vote the money back into the trust fund some time later. Is that not very much like what the bank teller always says when he takes trust funds-that something will happen later on and that the money will be returned? This government puts its hand on trust funds, casts them where it will, then says, "Oh well, parliament will have to return them in order to save the government."

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health

speechtext:
I think a very simple explanation can be given. It was recognized two years ago that certain organizations were carrying out certain duties on behalf of the

ex-service men. Parliament recognized that to the extent of appropriating a sum of money to recoup those organizations which had spent money in so serving the ex-service men. First of all, therefore, that principle was recognized. Last year a bill was introduced into this House making provision for the maintenance of the service bureau at headquarters in Ottawa and the amount of $100,000 was specified in the bill for the purpose. My right hon. friend has admitted-and it is of common knowledge-that this bill passed the House of Commons nemine contradicente-not a single word of opposition from anybody. Questions were asked as to how the board should be constituted, and so on, but the principle was recognized by the House of Commons of that time that canteen fund money could be used for the purpose of maintaining a service bureau.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
The point is that it is
not canteen fund money that is used at all; it is disablement fund money. That is the whole thing.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I am coming to that.
There are two trust funds, the disablement fund and the canteen funds. I hold that the disablement fund can better be used for this purpose than the canteen funds, and that is the view of Sir Arthur Currie. Sir Arthur Currie is of the opinion that unless parliament provides differently, the disablement fund could be put to no better use than that of supporting an adjustment bureau at headquarters. I say that the House of Commons recognized the principle of the maintenance of a service bureau at headquarters and that the House of Commons voted $100,000 for the purpose from the canteen funds. That the bill did not become law was not because the Senate rejected it on the ground of its not deserving their approval; the reasons were well known-they said they had not time to go into the matter fully. These facts being of common knowledge, am I to prevent the adjustment bureau from fulfilling the duties which have been recognized by the House, by withholding from them assistance available from the disablement fund? I would not take any money from the canteen funds for this purpose. Why? Because a bill was introduced in parliament, and although it was approved by the House of Commons it did not pass the Senate and was therefore not adopted by parliament. But after consultation with many who occupy high places among the returned soldiers I was advised that some money might be taken from the disablement fund for the purpose, it being

that no portion- of this sum of $100,000 which he expects to be appropriated from the canteen fund and placed under this central board of three trustees is going to be paid to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
If the trustees are willing
to reimburse the disablement fund, they may do it, and if they do not choose to reimburse the disablement fund the loan will not be paid, but the amount will have been spent for the benefit of the ex-service men. Does my hon. friend dispute that?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: In other words, the minister says that he is not going to exercise any coercion over these trustees, though he has already passed an order in council stating that he will tell these trustees that they must appropriate this $20,000 as soon as they are appointed. Now he says that he will not exercise any coercion over them, and if they refuse, the result will be that the trust funds which have been misappropriated and which belong to the disablement fund will never be repaid.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I do not agree with my hon. friend that the trust funds have been misappropriated in the sense that they have been taken away from the ex-service men.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: The word "misappropriated" has a peculiarly significant meaning. I have been looking it up in Crankshaw. It is not within the range of expressions that may be used in the House of Commons.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Any charge at all can be laid against a government, and it is against the government that we are laying the charge. You may lay a charge of misappropriation, or theft or anything else against the government.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I would call the right
hon. gentleman's attention-

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Perhaps the Chairman
will show me where, under the rules, this cannot be done.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I do not need to refer to the rules to substantiate the ruling that the expression that has been used is not within the compass of those that may properly be directed against a minister.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: All ministers are responsible for actions of the government, and so long as an expression is directed against the government there can be nothing unparliamentary about it.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I quite agree with that, but I disagree with the contention that a remark may be directed to a minister questioning the honesty of his own conduct.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
When I was interrupted I was about to point out that these moneys belong to the disablement fund and are unquestionably in trust; as recited here, they were subscribed by patriotic citizens during the war to be used generally in the making of small loans to pensioners and others in need of immediate assistance. There is the sole purpose of the fund; that is what it was created for. And here we have a portion of these moneys appropriated and paid to an organization, the minister being unable to give us any details whatever of what it was used for. He cannot tell us whether it was used for the purpose of paying salaries, nor can he assure us that there is any probability of its being returned. He admits, as he must admit in view of the terms of the order in council, that these moneys were taken out of the trust fund, contrary to the express object for which they were subscribed. He attempts to justify that course of action before this committee, yet cannot give us any assurance

Canteen Funds
that the moneys will be repaid, nor can he assure us that the trustees of the canteen fund when appointed will be trustees in fact, free from government control. It is a pretty mess that the minister has got himself into, as far as I can judge.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I merely rise to bring to the attention of the committee something that has taken place in previous years and which probably has been overlooked. I cannot really follow the line of reasoning of our friends to the right on this particular question; perhaps I may be able to follow them in other respects but not on this question. There seems to be a good deal of criticism of the action taken by the minister (Mr. Beland) in allocating certain sums, which were held in trust, to a representative of the Dominion Veterans' Alliance. Personally I would commend the minister on the judgment he used in this matter. It is a well known fact that the Veterans' Alliance have decided amongst themselves to appoint one of their number to speak on their behalf, and before all previous special parliamentary committees which have considered these various questions, the Dominion Veterans' Alliance have had a spokesman. In the majority of cases they have been represented by Mr. MacNeil, who has proved a very admirable representative.
I think that possibly this question has come up to-day much in the same way as a similar question was brought up in 1921, and it would be interesting if hon. members of the committee would refer to the final report on the second part of the investigation which was carried out by what has been called the Ralston commission. Looking over that report I find that the government of that day, that is to say, 1921, passed a good many orders in council along the same line. We need only refer to Nos. 2378, 3648, 3519, 3762, 3647 and many others, which have to do with the allocation by the government of certain funds that were held in trust.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Who would allocate them if the government did not?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
But the question came up nevertheless as to whether the government had the power to allocate funds which it held in trust and which were the property of the men throughout Canada at that time. As the leader of the opposition (Mr. Meighen) knows, the question arose in 1921 as to the right of the government to take to itself that authority, and in my opinion the present minister, in allocating say $25,000, in the way that has been indicated, can point to a very 50i
strong precedent established in 1921. I think it would be well for hon. gentlemen to read over these orders in council to which I have referred, inasmuch as the question did arise as to what authority the government had in the circumstances. Those moneys at that time were held in trust for the returned men throughout Canada.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Subject to the action of parliament.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Yes, and practically in the same manner as in the case of the present order in council which has come under discussion.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: The hon. member is not within a mile of the point.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I take it that the two things are similar.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Can the hon. member tell us what amounts were appropriated in 1921?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I should say, roughly speaking, about $100,000.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: For what purpose?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: The various reasons are set forth in the orders in council; moneys were given to every individual returned soldier organization for certain purposes. As I size up the present situation, I should say that there is some similarity between it and the condition I have described as existing in 1921. If the government had authority in the matter then, I should say the government would have the same authority now, subject to the approval of parliament.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I agree entirely with the hon. gentleman, but in the former case the government of the day published an order in council and used the canteen fund for the benefit of returned soldiers; in this case the government did not take that action, they went to the Carruthers fund.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Was not the canteen
fund at that date held in trust? And is not this practically the same thing?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, the hon.
member complains that he cannot follow the reasoning of this group to his right. I am afraid that I shall have to say in all deference to him that until he gets a lot closer to the subject he can never expect to follow our reasoning. He is off the line altogether. The canteen fund is in a sense a trust fund. This is a trust fund. But the difference is that the government is trustee of the canteen fund; it has nothing to do with this trust fund. I wonder if an officer of this govern-
Canteen Funds

ment, say the Deputy Minister of the Interior, were treasurer of the Red Cross fund, would the hon. gentleman say that the government would be quite justified in ordering that man to dip his hand into the Red Cross fund to help out the situation that the government wanted to help out at the moment? Does he think so?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I would hardly think
so. But I still question the right of the government in 1921 to dip their hand into the canteen fund.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
If the hon. member
questions the action of the government in 1921, why was he a party to the justification of it in voting the money? Because it was right. I am not questioning that action at all, I never did. This House, controlled by a government opposed to us, voted the money, and thereby ratified what we did. Therefore it is a little late now to question our action. The government had to determine, subject to the will of parliament, how to best carry out that trusteeship. The government was trustee, the fund was in the hands of the government and subject to the audit of the Auditor General. In determining what action to take we were subject to the ratification of this House. Here is a fund over which the government has no control at all; it is a fund in the hands of an individual, and the purposes for which it is to be applied are clearly set out in the order in council-for loans and pensions to individual disabled men. That is what the contributors to the fund wanted the money used for. But because the trustee happens to be one of its officers, this government says to that trustee, "Put your hand down in the treasury and give us this money, hand it over to the Veterans' Alliance, because we believe in the purposes of the Alliance."

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Had the trustee power to refuse in this case?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Yes, I say most frankly he should have refused, no matter who appointed 'him. A trustee has no justification whatever for taking dictation from the government; the only dictation he should submit to is the dictation of the deed of trust.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Can anyone here give us
the terms of the deed of trust?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Yes, it is recited in the order in council:
The Committee of the Privy Council have had before them a report dated 12th September, 1924, from the Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment, representing that the Assistant Deputy Minister of the Department of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment is the trustee of a fund known as the
(Mr. Meighen.]
Disablement Fund, which was contributed by patriotic citizens mainly during the years 1915 and 1916, and that this fund is being used generally for the purpose of small loans to pensioners and others who are in need of immediate assistance and who, in the opinion of the departmental investigations, would benefit by such assistance.
That is the purpose of the fund.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Of course, that does not
give the terms of the trust in full.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I have no doubt the
terms are set out more fully elsewhere, but this gives enough to make it clear that the fund was not intended, for example, for the purpose of a $25,000 loan to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance who were carrying on activities all over Canada, activities for the benefit of the men who were just as well as you and I. Is that a purpose within the meaning of the clause as there defined?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I am inclined to agree with you.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: It is the plainest possible breach of trust. The minister gets this money, over which he had no disposition at all, which does not go before the Auditor General, and consequently is not within the disposition of the government as such, and he says to the trustee, "Use that money for this purpose." Then we are asked to justify it because the funds over which we have control were disposed of in anticipation of the judgment of parliament.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
The order in council
states that these funds are being generally used for the purpose of assisting individual cases. Does the deed of trust specify that the funds shall be used only for that purpose, or is it simply indicated by the order in council that it is being used generally for that purpose? This seems to me to be an important point.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I have not seen the deed of trust, but on the minister's admission there is a private trustee, there is no trusteeship in the government. Consequently the government had no authority to order the trustee to do this at all. Further, if by any possibility the trustee were justified in using the money to this end, this order in council would never have been necessary. The fact that the order in council exists shows that there was a diversion of the trust fund, and the fact also that the Dominion Veterans' Alliance is to get this money back on a request, as it is put, of these trustees to be appointed, shows it is trust funds that have been diverted.

Canteen Funds

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I am going to ask the
minister three questions in the hope that he will be able to give me answers to them. These questions, I think, will show the difficult position in which he and the government are placed under certain circumstances. In the first place, suppose the House of Commons, or the Senate, or the Parliament of Canada at this session refuse to pass legislation dealing with the canteen fund, suppose they do as the Senate did last year, throw it out, where is the minister going to get the money to enable Mr. Scammell to recoup his trust fund which money he, on the order of one of his superior officers, loaned to the government to pay salaries or something of the sort? Second, suppose the legislation does pass and these trustees are appointed, and suppose then they refuse to pay back the money, saying, "We had nothing to do with the 125,000 spent last year; we are appointed to deal with the future, not with the past, and we refuse to pay back this money to the trust fund from which it was borrowed," where will the government get the money? Third, suppose that the government cannot get the money to pay it back-I do not know how the government can pay this money back except by getting the proposed legislation enacted and appointing trustees who wall be willing to pay it back-if the government do not get the money to pay it back to Mr. Scammell, what position would he be in? -because the order in council distinctly states that this money was in the hands of Mr. Scammell as trustee for the purpose of making small loans to disabled veterans. He would be S25,000 short, and he would certainly be liable personally to the trust fund for that money; I do not think there is any question about that. Will the minister answer those three questions?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: The matter reduced to its simplest form is that a loan has been made by Mr. Scammell to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance. That is the fact.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Even that fact is disputed.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
That the loan has been
made?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
No, the fact is disputed
by one of the officers of the Dominion Veterans' Alliance that they ever got the money.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: My hon. friend surely does not seriously contend that the money was not paid to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I seriously contend that
one of the officers of the-

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
If my hon. friend will
permit me to continue.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
My hon. friend asked me
a question; I was going to answer him.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: If the money has not been paid it is in the trust fund.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Not necessarily, it may
have been used for other purposes.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Well, it has been paid out. My hon. friend will admit that?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I think probably it has.
That is one thing we will admit.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: The money has been paid out as a consequence of Mr. Scammell consenting to make a loan to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance. That is admitted also?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Did he consent?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Surely he did; otherwise
the loan could not have been made.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
What about the order
in council?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: What order in council could force him to make the loan? The right hon. gentleman (Mr. Meighen) has stated twice in my hearing that the trustee could have objected and refused to make the loan. That is very clear. He made the loan. My hon. friend questions the payment of this money to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I question it-if the minister will allow me to correct him-on the statement of one of the officers who says that the Dominion Veterans' Alliance did not get the money. He does not say that some officer did not get it, but he does say that the Dominion Veterans' Alliance never had the handling of it.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Who was the officer?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I do not know that I need answer that.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Somebody must act for the Dominion Veterans' Alliance. You cannot pay the money to a piece of paper bearing on its face "Dominion Veterans' Alliance"; you must pay it to somebody who represents that organization, somebody who is authorized to act for the organization; in this instance I think it must be the secretary treasurer, though I am not absolutely sure about that. It has been made plain to the committee that six or seven different Dominion-wide organizations have got together and formed what is known as the Dominion Veterans' Alliance
Canteen Funds

with a president, a vice president and a secretary treasurer. Mr. MacNeil is the secretary treasurer of the Dominion Veterans' Alliance.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Is he secretary of that organization at the moment?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Yes, I think he is, and has been from the first. He happens to be at the same time, I think, secretary of the Great War Veterans' Association. But it is not for me to say whether he should be in either one place or the other; he happens to be there, and the loan has been made to him. If it is not paid back into the trust fund the trustee will be in the position of having made a loan in the interests of ex-service men to assist them in presenting their claims-disabled men who have claims to present to the department and to the Board of Pension Commissioners. The spirit of the trust is preserved. Does my right hon. friend say that the spirit of the trust is not preserved?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I say the spirit of the
trust has been brazenly violated.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I do not agree with my
right hon. friend. He is very insistent in his assertion that we have violated the trust. Does he say that the canteen fund could be regularly disposed of without action of the Canadian parliament?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
The canteen fund, like
any other trust fund in the disposition of the government-for the government is trustee of all its funds-can regularly and constitutionally be disposed of in anticipation of parliament. The only question is, are the circumstances so exigent as to demand it- that is all. But that law does not apply and that rule does not apply to a fund over which the government has no control.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
The government did not
make the loan; the government did not take the money from the trust fund. Representations were made to the minister in charge that the maintenance of a service bureau would be impossible unless assistance was given. The minister in charge, who happened to be myself, asked the man in charge of the fund to make a loan to these people. I did that, and I am not sorry for it; I would do it again because it is right. The loan has been made, and it has served what purpose? It has helped the Dominion Veterans' Alliance, or the men who are in it, to discharge important and useful duties to returned men generally in Canada. That is what has been done with the money.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Was that why the money was given to this trustee?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I believe so.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
"To discharge important
and useful duties to returned men generally in Canada"?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Surely, that is the spirit
of it.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Well, if the minister cannot see the distinction I am afraid there is no use of proceeding further. That was not the spirit of it at all. What is the sense of talking about the spirit and the letter and all the rest of it? The thing is as plain as words ever were. It is one thing to devote money to a trusteeship, to a trust for the purpose of returned men generally, disabled and undisabled alike, the well-off and the poor alike-that is one thing; but it is a wholly different thing to devote money to a trust for the purposes of disabled men only, for loans to small pensioners and the like who are disabled. Yet the minister stands up and says: We have helped the returned men generally by this action; I am proud of it and I would do it again.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Has not my right hon. friend missed something just as important as the stress he lays upon the making of loans to pensioners only? If the order in council contains a proper quotation of the trust, and I take it that it does-

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I did not say pensioners only; I said disabled men.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
My right
hon. friend is stressing the point that this trust fund was for one purpose only, that of loans to and assistance to pensioners and others in need of funds.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Disabled men.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Yes, but it also says, "to others who are in need of immediate assistance," and it says that the decision is not altogether in the hands of the trustee. I would prefer not to say very much about this until I have seen a copy of the trust itself, but I take it that this is a fairly definite statement of what is contained in the trust. Not only that, but it goes on further to say, "who in the opinion of the departmental investigations." Surely my right hon. friend will not contend that one individual, in the person of Mr. Scammell, had the absolute disposition of that fund, to whom he might seek to give it? Loans are specified to individuals and others, and the investigation is to be departmental.

Canteen Funds

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Does my hon. friend suggest to the committee that this fund, which is known as the disablement fund, can legally be given in any way to men who are not disabled at all?

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I do not
know, because I have not seen the deed of trust.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Is the minister not bound to know that before he can support this proposal?

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I am quoting the very words here, in the preamble.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
The preamble intimates
clearly it cannot.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I differ from my hon. friend. It says "and to others who would benefit by such assistance."

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Disabled pensioners and
others.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Here is the document. I will hand it to my right hon. friend.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Very good; I have it here too. I do not think it could be called a "disablement fund" to start with if it is a fund for the undisabled. If what the Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment says is right, then there is no need of this order at all.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I am not
raising that point.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Here is what it says:
This fund is being used generally for the purpose of small loans to pensioners and others who are in need of immediate assistance and who, in the opinion of the departmental investigations, would benefit by such assistance.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: That is the point.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Very good; the trustee
gets the benefit of the departmental investigations.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Does my right hon. friend
still maintain that it is a fund to pensioners?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: No, I never said it was.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
My right hon. friend just
said that.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: No, no; I say it is not for the undisabled-that is, from all the indications here; I have never seen the deed of trust, as I have repeated over and over again.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
All who are war disabled
are war pensioners.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I know some who are
not; and there would be disabled men who would be disabled before they would be pensioners, and the fund could be used for them. But I have not seen the deed of trust. I know this, that a fund known as a "disablement fund" may be presumed not to be for the undisabled. Secondly, I know that if it were for all alike, for general purposes, there would have been no need of this order in council at all.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
As far as I am concerned
I will say this: No loan was made from the disablement fund with my consent or at my request before I had secured from the chief donator and Sir Arthur Currie an expression of their views, and their view is that it can be used for an adjustment bureau.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Does the minister say
he has that from Mr. Carruthers?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Yes, it was secured from
him.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Is it in writing?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I think I can have it in
writing.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I would be very glad
to get it.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: At all events it was requested from him and he expressed his view, as did Sir Arthur Currie also. Does my hon. friend say Sir Arthur Currie did not?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I do not know anything about that, nor do I care. What matters is the deed of trust, and that deed of trust Sir Arthur Currie and no other man can change.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
My hon. friend is an
adroit and skilful lawyer-

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Not at all.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Yes, everybody will grant
him that, but upon this point, although he has used all his adroitness and his skill, he cannot succeed in putting the minister wrong. My view is that the Dominion Veterans' Alliance was discharging a useful and important duty to pensioners and to other service men in need of assistance.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Nobody denies that.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Well then, we agree perfectly. The loan was requested from Mr. Scammell-I could not authorize the loan- for the purpose of discharging those very purposes.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Is Mr. Scammell satisfied,
if the legislation does not pass and the money
Canteen Funds

does not come back, that he has lived up to his duties as trustee of this fund?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I think so.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Then, if the minister has finished, I would like to differ. I am not an adroit lawyer as he says my right hon. leader is.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Oh, don't complain.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I am not complaining;
I am rather glad I am not. But I want to point out that the order in council distinctly says, if this is taken from the charter or trust deed, that this disablement fund is being used generally for purposes of small loatis. The Minister of the Interior read just beyond that. It is loans to pensioners and others who are in immediate need.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Read it all.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
The minister would not
call $25,000 a small loan.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
They are small loans if
they are spread over two or three years.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
It was not spread over two and a half years. The smallest amount paid out was $5,000. The small loans referred to here are loans of ten or twenty or thirty or at the most fifty dollars to' pensioners who have got into difficulty. The minister knows full well that very many times a pensioner for some reason or other does not get his pension when it is due, not due to any fault on the part of the officials, but that sometimes happens. I have had dozens of chaps come into my office whose pensions were two or three months over-
5 p.m. due, and then all would be paid the arrears in one cheque. I am not blaming the department for that; it would probably happen if I were in charge. But take a man like that who gets into difficulties over his board bill and needs immediate assistance. He can come to this fund for assistance to the extent, I would say, of $25, or $50 at the most. It was cases of that kind that were spoken of as small loans, not $3,000 or $5,000 for another department altogether. If the minister says he is perfectly satisfied with what he has done, and would be perfectly satisfied if the money was not returned, I think Mr. Scammell must be very uneasy; if I were in his shoes I would be very nervous about the disablement fund if the minister would be perfectly satisfied if the government did not pay the amount back.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Mr. Scammell is like my
hon. friend; he is not nervous,

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I think he should be nervous. I hope the minister will bring that trust deed down; he has had plenty of time to bring it down already and he should let us know exactly what that money was for. When the trust deed is here we shall be able to discuss the matter much more intelligently. If only small loans were to be made, there has been an absolute breach of trust in giving out $25,000 from that fund for any other purpose than the purpose laid out here. I venture the assertion that the minister when outlining this order in council, if the charter or trust deed had permitted these moneys to be used for such purposes as this, would have shown his good common sense 'by putting that in the order in council; but it distinctly says it was for small loans. So unless the trust deed shows a good deal more than this shows, there has been an absolute breach of trust in handing out $25,000 to any organization.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Read it.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I will read the whole thing to put it on record:
The committee of the Privy Council have had before them a report dated 12th September, 1924, from the Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment representing that the Assistant Deputy Minister of the Department of Soldiers' Civil Re-estab-lis foment-
That is Mr. Scammell.
is the trustee of a fund known as the disablement fund which was contributed by patriotic citizens mainly during the years 1915 and 1916 and that this fund is being used generally for the purpose of small loans to pensioners and others who are in need of immediate assistance and who, in the opinion of the departmental investigations, would benefit by such assistance.
I do not see any other interpretation, but that what was meant was small loans of ten or twenty or thirty or perhaps up to fifty dollars to pensioners or others in need of immediate assistance. Certainly by no stretch of the imagination can you include under that clause payments for the salaries, which I presume this money was used for, of the officers of the Dominion Veterans' Alliance or of the Great War Veterans' Association or any other body.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: The speech of my hon. friend who has just sat down (Mr. Manion) is based entirely on the alleged contents of a document about which this committee has been talking for over an hour, but which it has never seen and knows nothing about.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
That is the minister's fault.

Canteen Funds

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: The minister dealing with this question cannot get papers out of his office in such an easy way as my hon. friend thinks. The whole question is, under what terms and conditions does Mr. Scammell hold this money known as the disablement fund?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: He is in the gallery.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I do not care where he is; what difference does it make? Surely this committee is going to wait until it sees this document which constitutes the trust deed before we express an opinion one way or the other. I think, Mr. Chairman, we might well have saved the time that has been taken up by this discussion for the last hour, in which suggestions and insinuations have been made here and there as to what was done with this money, in view of the fact that nobody in this committee knows what the terms of the trust are.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Would it not be better if the usual procedure had been followed that obtains in the case of resolutions of this kind and estimates in committee, when the minister has one of his officials on the floor to advise him on questions which we all frankly admit it is difficult for the minister to anticipate.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
That is
something that every minister will have to decide for himself. The point I wanted to make is this: I think this committee might well have awaited the receipt of this trust deed and found out its terms and conditions before expressing a hasty opinion. I want to say further that it is a fact that Sir Arthur Currie, about whose interest in this matter nobody can have any doubt, has stated that he knew no better purpose for which the money in this disablement fund could be used than maintaining this adjustment service.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Does that make it right?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I think hon. gentlemen might well have hesitated to make insinuations when he approved of the money being used in that way.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Have you a written opinion from Sir Arthur Currie?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: If we have, do you agree with it?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I am very doubtful if he gave it. I have too high an opinion of his good judgment to think he would give
such an opinion, if the details were explained to him. I would like to see an opinion from Sir Arthur Currie in writing. Has the department such a document?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Hon. members seem to have got into a suspicious frame of mind. When I say that Sir Arthur Currie stated that he knew no better purpose for which the fund could be used than this scheme hon. members say they do not believe he said it. I say he did say it, and I say further-and I think the committee will agree with me-that the proper way is to wait and see what occurred with this trust deed.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
Assume this is a trust
for disabled soldiers, does the minister suggest that by any stretch of the imagination these funds should be loaned to the War Veterans' Association for the purpose of paying salaries which the members of that association have not interest enough to pay?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: My hon. friend is a lawyer and a very distinguished one, and he knows that he could not expect me or any other person to express an opinion upon any question with so many presumptions and whereases as he has put in this question. I will wait until I see the document.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
If in the opinion of the minister, the government and Sir Arthur Currie the terms of the trust agreement have not been violated, and the money has been appropriated to a proper cause, why pay it back? Why not leave it as it is? Why pass such an order as has come to light since this debate began? And why dip into the canteen fund to take money to pay back this money which has been-the word " misappropriated " has been used but has been objected	to-improperly withdrawn
from the disablement fund? If the government was not doing wrong in using that fund, why pay it back? Let it go. Eventually that disablement fund must be expended and dissipated. If reasonable and proper expenditure has been made of part of it, let it go, and if not why go into the canteen funds to get money to pay it back? Let the government put it in the estimates and put it through in the regular way. There is no reason on earth why the canteen fund should be used to pay back the money paid to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
My hon. friend will remember that a certain amount, namely $100,000, was set aside in the bill last year for
Canteen Funds

the purpose of maintaining an adjustment bureau, and that bill never became law. It was understood to be the unanimous desire of the House of Commons that $100,000 should be used for the purpose of maintaining a service bureau. The trustee of the fund, without questioning the use of a certain amount of money for the maintenance of the bureau, suggested perhaps that it should be repaid to him, because he makes loans with the idea of being repaid, and the provision in the order in council is, if possible, that this trustee should be paid the loan he has made at my suggestion.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: What is the total amount in that fund?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: And this is 25 per cent of the total fund-a small loan.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Although the amount of the fund is now $100,000, there is a great deal of money which has been loaned, and some small loans are outstanding and some written off.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: What was the biggest loan previously made?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I have no idea.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: When the minister brings the agreement this evening, will he also bring with him the details of the expenditure of $25,000 and the exact name and position held by the payee of the cheque?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I will give the name of the payee, of course.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Will the minister answer my question?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I will give the name of the payee. I cannot supply him with all the information he desires.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Can he supply the committee now or at a later time with the details of the expenditure of this money advanced to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I will try to do that.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Did I understand the minister to inform the committee that the House of Commons passed a resolution for the distribution of the canteen fund before any loan was made by the trustee of the disablement fund to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: No, I never said that.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Will the minister give me the date when Sir Arthur Currie approved of this scheme ?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I will try and get it.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Is it in writing?

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: It is in writing.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Will the minister bring that letter.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I do not say I will bring the letter, but I will quote the passage that refers to that matter.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: We want the letter.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: If Sir Arthur Currie treats with subjects which have no relation to the disablement fund, my hon. friend would not insist on my producing that.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Perhaps not, but I can hardly conceive of his dealing with an important matter of a trustee like this in the body of a general letter. It is the rule of the House that if the minister lays on the table of the House any letter or document, or reads it, he must read the whole of it.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: Was the deed of trust submitted to Sir Arthur Currie when he gave, his opinion? I can understand him expressing a view as to what might be done with a certain fund which was not ear marked in some way, but if it was to be disposed of according to the terms of a trust agreement, one would think that he should see that agreement before he could express an opinion that would be of any value. I would like to know from my hon. friend (Mr. Beland) or from the Minister of Militia and Defence (Mr. Macdonald) whether he ever saw the agreement.

speakerposition: Minister of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment; Minister presiding over the Department of Health
maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I cannot give an answer to the question as to whether he ever saw it.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I suppose my hon. friend will agree with me that if he had not seen the trust agreement his opinion would be of no value. The Minister of Militia and Defence has said that he or no other intelligent person Should be asked to give an opinion without seeing the trust agreement; therefore it is most vital to know whether he saw it, because if he did not his opinion would not be of any consequence. I want the minister to bring certain papers with him. I take it for granted that when a loan involving $25,000 is made by the trustee of the fund there will be a contract of some description under which the money will be repaid whether with or without interest, and stating when it shall be repaid and by whom. I would ask him to bring such a contract with him if there is one. You can hardly imagine that the minister or the trustee on his advice would loan that money

Canteen Funds
to any association without some document providing for repayment.
The minister points out that these loans are made under the trust agreement. I would ask the minister to look at the very words of the first paragraph of the order in council- and I am assuming they were used intentionally and deliberately; that they properly indicate in a measure at all events the purposes of the trust-and say if it is not perfectly plain that the intention there is that the trustees should make these loans to individuals for the benefit of individuals, and if he can find anything in the language used in the order in council which would warrant the giving of that money to an association and not to the individuals who are intended to benefit by it.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
If my hon. friend will more closely scrutinize the order in council from which he is quoting, he will see that it does not purport to quote the terms of the trust deed, but that it goes on to say that this money under the disablement fund is now being used for the purpose of making small loans.
Mr. BOA'S: I absolutely agree with what the minister says, but I think I have a right to assume that in so using it, they are using it in accordance with the declaration of trust, and surely the minister would be one of the last to ask me to come to any different conclusion. When, in the Privy Council, of which he is a member, this language is used, surely he is not going to suggest that the Minister of Soldiers' Civil Reestablishment (Mr. Boland1) in introducing this order in council and asking to have it passed is intimating that this money is being used for purposes not authorized by the declaration of trust?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: No. .

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: If it is for purposes authorized by the trust -as are indicated in the order in council, surely it is manifest that the money is intended for individual benefit and use and not for the use of any association.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: That might be only one of the purposes of the trust. There might be many other purposes in the trust-We had better wait until we see the trust deed.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I think we are wasting time, because it is very unlikely that this resolution will pass before the minister has brought down certain information. A couple of weeks ago I asked the minister whether
or not an order in council had been passed diverting funds from the canteen fund for other -purposes. The answer of the minister was no. If, however, the minister is right in his premises to-day, that answer was wrong, because he is seeking to recoup the disablement fund from the canteen fund. At least the order in council refers to the canteen fund indirectly. The request has been made to-day by myself and others that the trust deed be produced before we go any further with this debate. I believe the minister mow nods his head when he says that $25,000 has been paid. Only an hour or two ago he would not admit that $15,000 had been paid over to the Dominion Veterans' Alliance. I should like to -ask how much has been -paid, -to whom, on whose recommendation and for what purpose it was paid. I should also like to ask the minister if he can produce a record of any case in which this government or any previous government has passed an order in council directing a private trustee to divert funds whether for the -benefit of -the government or anybody else.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: I do not know th-at any older in council has been -passed prior to this, disposing of the disablement fund or any portion of it. But I was referring a few minutes ago to the canteen fund and my right hon. friend stopped me at a point when I was asking him whether he thought it was regular that -the government should apportion to soldiers' organizations large amounts of the canteen funds without the authority of parliament. The canteen funds are made up of moneys which belong to the returned men, to all those who served overseas. By what stretch of imagination can the leader of the opposition contend that it is regular to dispose of the canteen funds by order in council when this parliament is sitting, and every year when it had been sitting in 1919, in 1920 and in 1921, only a month, I think, before the first disposal of the canteen fund was m-ad'e? Does he think this is quite regular?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
I will answer very
directly, but first of all I cannot help commenting on the minister's wondering as to the morality of disposing of the canteen funds under the government's charge, but having no doubt about the morality of disposing of the disablement fund which was not under their charge at all. I have stated repeatedly that any fund under the charge of the government may be disposed of in anticipation of the will of parliament. There is no hindrance save that the Auditor General must be
Canteen Funds

convinced that the exigent circumstances require it to be done. If the government fails to get the authority of parliament for what it has done, the government goes out of office. That applies to the canteen fund as well as to all other funds of which the government is trustee. This House at this session will be asked repeatedly to vote money which this government has paid out of funds of which it is trustee in anticipation of the will of parliament. That is what was done in 1921. That is what this government is doing this year. That, I do not criticize. It is all a matter of the nature of the circumstances which demand it. This is a matter in another category wholly, as I have sought to explain. I do not wish to prolong the discussion further. I am only too anxious to see the terms of his declaration of trust. What we have now indicates that a breach has been committed. When we get the full terms it will not matter what anybody, however dignified, may have said as to the merits of the Dominion Veterans' Alliance. I had never attacked the Dominion Veterans' Alliance or any organization under it. They serve a purpose that is perfectly laudable and right, but because a fund is a trust fund devoted to a certain purpose, you cannot justify diverting it to another by merely saying that the other purpose is very laudable and good.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext: At the rate the government of the day, during the few months prior to November 1921, were disbursing the funds they held in trust for the returned men, the minister, had they been returned to power, would not have been able to bring a measure before parliament to provide for the disposition of any $2,000,000 because the late government were paying out these funds at the rate of from $25,000 to $50,000 a month. Mr. BOYS: Anything wrong with that?

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
In my opinion, yes.
I was not here at the time.

maintopic: QUESTIONS ON ORDERS OF THE DAY UNANSWERED
speechtext:
The hon. member was
here when that was ratified.
Progress reported.

The House in committee of Supply, Mr. Gordon in the chair.
Public Works-Salaries and contingencies, $689,655.
lion. J. H. KING (Kootenay, Minister of Public Works):	Perhaps I had better make
a brief statement in explanation of the items before the committee, comparing them with the estimate passed last year. There is a reduction of S18,665. The estimate last year 
was $633,320 for salaries, but we aTe asking this year for $614,655 for the same purpose. There has been a decrease of four in the number of positions, due to the following reasons. Ten positions were dropped from civil government owing to retirements and resignations. This is offset in part by two new appointments, one a position which was dropped last year but which is revived for 1925-26, and three transfers from the Ottawa building repairs vote. Two new positions, are provided for namely, a clerk-typist and an office appliance operator; but the position was revived of assistant to general superintendent of telegraph service. This makes a net decrease of four. It might be wise to explain how the reduction is made up, accounting for the reduction in the estimate this year. Three positions were reclassified, at a reduction of $1,180; one vacancy was reduced to the minimum, making a reduction of $360; there were five deaths accounting for a saving of $1,290; there were ten resignations, accounting for $9,750. twelve retirements, $15,535, twenty promotions in connection with which there was a decrease of $5,970; and one position abolished at $300, making a total decrease of $34,385.
